newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans to upgrade refineries and expand base.
newsitem.headline: China plans to upgrade refineries and expand base.

text.p: China plans to upgrade refineries along its coast and the Yangtze river to create major bases capable of refining imported high sulphur crude oil, the China Economic Times said on Tuesday.

Some companies with suitable conditions for the investment have been encouraged to refine more high sulphur crudes, the newspaper quoted Ma Chengquan, vice director of the Raw Materials and Comprehensive Utilisation department of the State Planning Commission, as saying.
"Some coastal refineries with deep water wharves will be revamped and expanded to make them into major bases for refining and processing imported crude oil," Ma said without giving details.
China's oil production has been unable to keep pace with rapidly growing domestic demand and imports are widely expected to rise in the years ahead to fill the gap.
China's domestically produced oil has a low sulphur content and Chinese refineries are being pushed to spend large sums to refine high sulphur crude.
Oil industry specialists say much of that oil will come from the Middle East.

China's Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co Ltd, based in Ningbo in eastern China's Zhejiang province, has said it has been encouraged to boost its ability to refine high sulphur curds in line with government policy.
